exposure: Gestational age at delivery (<41 weeks, >=41 weeks)
outcome: Neonatal trauma (brachial plexus birth palsy, fractures)
Asphyxic sequelae (severe asphyxia, cerebral damage, fetal/infant death)
cohort: 66,885 deliveries occurring at or beyond 37 weeks gestation at two delivery units in Stockholm, Sweden between 2002 and 2009, including 3,343 LGA pregnancies.
finding: While antenatal identification of LGA did not reduce the overall risk of severe adverse outcomes in a unit using expectant management of LGA, it was associated with a lower risk of neonatal trauma in infants delivered after 41 weeks gestation.
mod_finding: For fetuses with an expected birth weight > 5000 g, planned cesarean delivery was associated with a lower risk of brachial plexus birth palsy compared to planned vaginal delivery.
gest_age: All deliveries were at or beyond 37 weeks gestation.
birth_weight: Infants were classified as appropriate-for-gestational age (AGA) or large-for-gestational age (LGA). Expected birth weight was also considered.
